description: Brand registry for Campaign OS. Each brand has its own voice bible, hooks bank, meme bank, FAQ templates, GBP templates, and asset namespace. Brand is the top-level partition — everything else (campaigns, hooks, memes, captions) belongs to exactly one brand. To onboard a new brand: copy any existing brand block, give it a unique id, fill in the voice/positioning/visual fields, and Campaign OS will isolate its data automatically.

swing-shack.positioning: Premium indoor golf experience in Johannesburg — TrackMan, fittings, coaching, memberships.
swing-shack.audience: Golfers in JHB aged 28–55 who care about getting better, not just looking good.

notes.how_brands_partition: Every campaign, asset, hook, meme, caption, GBP post, FAQ, scheduled item and published item carries a brand_id field (or inherits it from its campaign). When a brand is selected in the UI, every endpoint filters its data by brand_id. The schedule and review queue are brand-scoped. The calendar shows only the selected brand by default, with an 'all brands' option.
onboarding_new_brand: 1. Add a new brand block to brands.json with a unique id.
2. Add the matching voice entry to voice_bible.json#voices/<brand-id> with the same label.
3. Run the bootstrap flow (POST /api/brands/<brand-id>/bootstrap) to scaffold campaign-data.json with brand partition.
4. The brand appears in the picker immediately.
asset_partition_rules: campaigns[].brand_id = the brand that owns the campaign
campaigns[].assets[].brand_id = inherited from the parent campaign at creation time (immutable afterwards)
scheduled-items[].scheduled[].brand_id = captured at schedule-time from the source asset
Hooks/memes/captions generated via /api/intel/generate_* scope to the selected brand's voice by default
